Quick numbers from my side after modeling Samir's CSV:
- Baseline (current run-rate): ~18M tokens / month.
- Burst days (if weekly, averaged): adds ~55M incremental tokens / month.
- Cost to Redwood at current infra mix (g4x + reserved pools): ~$0.018/token marginally for burst hours; long-run settled margin supports offering a pilot pass-through at $0.023/token.

Options we can present:
A) 90-day Burst Pilot: +100M burst credit bucket, priced at $0.023/token, refundable against next-term commit up to 50% of allowed overage. Fast to sign; minimal infra change.
B) Tiered Commit: Move Helion up one tier (x2 baseline commit) with an automated 10% burst reserve and a reduced unit price of $0.017/token for baseline tokens and $0.020 for overflow. Requires 60-day lead for Dedicated capacity if they want strict latency guarantees.
C) Hybrid: Baseline commit bump (x1.4) + temporary burst credit (50M) to cover Q4. Lower near-term cash outlay; preserves flexibility.

I ran these against Helion's current spend and the pilot keeps their net delta small while giving time to confirm whether bursts are sticky. Monica, ops — does the hybrid change raise operational constraints (autoscale etc.)?

—Ben
